blocks.content: Democracy is not merely a form of government; it is primarily a mode of associated living, of conjoint communicated experience.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Challenges to national integration primarily stem from regionalism, communalism, casteism, and linguistic divides.
Socio-economic inequalities and poverty act as major hindrances to democratic consolidation and equitable development.
Good governance requires addressing corruption, institutional red-tapism, and ensuring administrative transparency.
Internal security threats and insurgencies pose significant challenges to state authority and public order.

rows: Friction between Centre and States, demands for autonomy
Erosion of secular fabric, public disorder
Misallocation of resources, loss of public trust in institutions

items: Frequently tested: Conceptual distinction between regionalism, regional identity, and federal autonomy.
High probability: Key statutory bodies and constitutional measures aimed at curbing corruption and administrative inefficiency.
Key focus: Constitutional provisions under Article 355 and Article 356 addressing internal disturbance and emergency situations.
